title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Among regular Dutch primary schools, is the neighbourhood composition of four-year-old intake associated with that of pupils already enrolled in the previous year, after accounting for where families live?
Level: inference. If families consider who already attends a school, small differences in pupil composition could reinforce themselves over time. This question explores whether school choice might contribute to lasting segregation beyond differences in where families live.

title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Datasets
We use four public datasets:

DUO pupil origins (2022–2023): pupil counts by school location and home postcode (PC4). We use these to describe where each school’s pupils live.
DUO school totals (2022–2023): total enrolment per school location. We use these to check how much of each school’s enrolment our data cover.
CBS postcode population (2022): resident counts by migration background and PC4. We combine these with pupil origins to describe schools’ neighbourhood composition.
DUO pupils by age and postcode (2023): pupil counts by age, school, and home postcode. We check whether four-year-old counts can support a later analysis of intake, particularly given suppressed small counts.

title: Assignment 2.1: School composition and school choice
text:
Exploratory process

Data and cleaning
The download script caches the source files. Functions in R/ then prepare, inspect, and plot the data.


Code
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

source("scripts/download.R")
source("R/prepare.R")
source("R/plots.R")

data <- prepare_data(paths)
intake <- check_intake(paths[["intake"]])
schools_2023 <- filter(data$schools, year == 2023)
selected <- filter(schools_2023, eligible)
#' Format counts with thousands separators.
format_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)


One row in the DUO pupil-origins data is a school–postcode–year; one plotted observation is a school location. School codes stay as text to preserve leading zeros. We restrict exploration to regular primary schools in 2022 and 2023 and join CBS by the home postcode, never the school’s address.
The neighbourhood composition proxy is the pupil-weighted average of the share of residents in CBS’s historical “non-western migration background” category in pupils’ home postcodes. It describes neighbourhoods, not individual pupils’ backgrounds. Both enrolment years use CBS 2022 so that postcode population changes do not drive the comparison.
Suppressed DUO counts (-1) remain missing. Only exact counts with a valid CBS match and at least 50 postcode residents enter the weighted average. We require at least 50 matched pupils per school and coverage of at least 80% of its total enrolment. These are exploratory quality rules; omitted pupils may differ from those observed.


Code
plot_coverage(data$schools)









Of 6,150 regular primary school locations in 2023, 3 lack a usable total and 5,656 pass both quality rules. Overall median coverage is 94.4%. Coverage combines count suppression, unusable postcodes, and missing CBS values; it is not a pure postcode match rate.


First patterns


Code
plot_composition(data$schools)









The middle half of included schools spans 4.0% to 16.3%. This variation makes the question worth investigating, but may reflect residential segregation and geography as well as school choice.


Code
plot_persistence(data$pairs)









Among 5,536 schools meeting the rules in both years, the median absolute change is 0.07 percentage points. The 7 orange triangles flag changes larger than five points for closer inspection, not automatic exclusion. Large changes could also arise from mergers or changing data coverage.


Decisions for the next stage
We also checked DUO’s October 2023 file by age and home postcode. Among 28,607 school–postcode cells with at least one four-year-old, 69.9% are suppressed as <5. This is the share of cells, not pupils. Age four is a proxy for intake, not an exact record of new enrolments. Small flows will therefore need a defensible treatment before modelling.

Keep neighbourhood composition as an explicitly labelled proxy; avoid claims about individual families or a school’s quality.
Examine four-year-old intake separately from existing pupils. Most pupils remain enrolled between years, so persistence in total enrolment is expected and does not demonstrate feedback.
Check school continuity and coverage before interpreting large changes; compare results under stricter coverage rules.
For the later inference, account for home-postcode and school differences and existing recruitment links. Show estimated associations with uncertainty; these exploratory plots do not answer the causal question.



Sources and reproducibility
DUO pupil origins, DUO school totals, DUO pupils by age and postcode, and CBS table 83503NED. The first knit downloads these public sources; later knits reuse local copies. No raw data is committed. Source releases may be revised. Code: thatmariia/bdst_dv.
